## Measures {#sec-measures}

Every method gives a set of draws of the weights: 4,000 per PUMA for the HMC
reference, the VB families and IPF multinomial, and a single fit for IPF. Each
draw is a complete synthetic population for one PUMA. For each published cell
(a table category in one block group or tract), we summarise a method's draws
of that cell's allocated count by the posterior mean, the posterior median and
the 5th and 95th percentiles, which bound the method's 90% posterior interval.

Unless stated otherwise, cell-level measures are pooled over the leaf cells of
the four PUMAs. Leaf cells are a table's published categories; its totals and
subtotals are left out, since they are sums of the leaves. Measures against
published values use *sampled* cells only: cells with a nonzero published
estimate and a sampling variance. This excludes published zeros, whose variance
is modelled. A published value $Y$ has standard error
$\mathrm{SE} = \mathrm{MOE}/1.645$, because the ACS publishes margins of error
at the 90% level.

### Fit and accuracy against published values

These measures appear in Tables 2 and 3 and in Figures C and D.

$|z|$ and its 90th percentile
:   For each cell, $|z| = |\bar m - Y| / \mathrm{SE}$, the distance between the
    method's posterior mean $\bar m$ and the published value, in published
    standard errors. We report the 90th percentile of $|z|$ over cells
    ("$|z|$ p90"). This summarises the cells a method fits worst without being
    set by a single extreme cell.

Coverage
:   The share of cells whose published value lies inside the method's 90%
    posterior interval. On the fitted (constraint) cells the published values
    were used in fitting, so coverage has no nominal level: even for the exact
    posterior it depends on how strongly each cell's own estimate determines
    its posterior. On held-out cells the interval is for the true count, while
    the published value also carries sampling error, so coverage below 0.90 is
    expected even for a correct model.

Half-width / MOE
:   The 90% interval's half-width over the published margin of error, median
    over cells: how wide the method's uncertainty is compared with the survey's
    own.

Interval score
:   The interval score of @gneiting2007, in published SEs, averaged over cells.
    The predictive interval for the published value is centred on the posterior
    mean. Its half-width $h_{\mathrm{pred}} = \sqrt{h^2 + (1.645\,\mathrm{SE})^2}$
    combines the posterior half-width $h$ with the published value's sampling
    error. The score is
    $$
    \frac{2h_{\mathrm{pred}} + (2/0.10)\max\left(|\bar m - Y| - h_{\mathrm{pred}},\; 0\right)}{\mathrm{SE}}.
    $$
    It rewards intervals that are narrow and contain the published value, so it
    judges centre and spread together. Lower is better. A method that knew
    every true count exactly would score about 4.13.

Held-out cells come from ACS tables not used in fitting. They are grouped as
related or less related to the constraint tables, at block-group and tract
level.

### Agreement with the reference posterior

These measures appear in Table 4 and Figure E. On the fitted leaf cells, each
method is compared with the HMC reference at the same $\alpha$; there the
reference is exactly the target the methods approximate. IPF, which has no
$\alpha$, is compared with each $\alpha$'s reference.

Median difference
:   $|\tilde m - \tilde m_{\mathrm{ref}}| / s_{\mathrm{ref}}$: the distance
    between the method's and the reference's posterior medians, in reference
    standard deviations. We report its median over cells (the typical cell) and
    its 99th percentile (the worst-centred cells). Zero is perfect.

Width ratio
:   The method's 90% interval width over the reference's. We report its median
    and its 10th percentile (the most overconfident cells). One is right; below
    one, the method is overconfident.

Pareto $\hat k$
:   For methods with a density (the VB families and MAP + Laplace), the shape
    parameter of Pareto-smoothed importance sampling applied to the importance
    ratios $\log \pi - \log q$, one per fit [@vehtari2024]. We report the median
    and range over PUMAs. Following @yao2018, $\hat k < 0.5$ indicates a good
    approximation, 0.5--0.7 an acceptable one, and $\hat k > 0.7$ an unreliable
    one.

### Usability of the draws

These measures appear in Table 5 and Figures A and B. They treat each draw as a
population that a user would analyse; they are computed per draw and pooled
over draws and PUMAs.

D/H, distinct household records per household
:   In a block group with $H$ published occupied households (ACS table B25003,
    owners plus renters), let $s_r$ be household record $r$'s share of the
    block group's households in the draw. Then
    $$
    D = \sum_r \left[1 - (1 - s_r)^H\right]
    $$
    is the expected number of distinct records among $H$ households drawn
    independently by those shares, and $D/H$ lies in $(0, 1]$. A value of one
    means every household is a different record; a small value means a few
    records are copied many times. It is computed for block groups with more
    than 100 published households. For each draw we take the smallest over its
    block groups (its worst block group) and the median (its typical one).
    Table 5 reports the median over draws of the smallest D/H, and the share of
    draws whose smallest D/H is below 0.025, about half the smallest any HMC
    reference draw reached (0.054).

Effective number of records
:   $n_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/\sum_r s_r^2$, the effective sample size of
    @kish1965 applied to the block group's shares. We report the same summaries
    as for D/H, and the share of draws with $n_{\mathrm{eff}} < 10$ in some
    block group.

Walls
:   The share of draws in which a single cell, one household record in one
    block group, holds more than 1% of the PUMA's population $N$.

Household count $|z|$
:   For each block group, the draw's allocated occupied households against the
    published B25003 total, in standard errors. The SE is the square root of
    the summed variances of the owner and renter cells; their covariance is
    ignored. We report the median over draws of each draw's largest $|z|$, and
    the share of draws whose largest exceeds 5.

### Cost

Table 1 and Figure C report minutes per PUMA, the mean over the four PUMAs,
split into fitting (raking, MAP, or MAP + VB; for HMC, the VB fit that whitens
it) and sampling.
